fields.meta_title: Newsletter Landing Page Builder and Examples | Emergent
fields.meta_description: See newsletter landing page examples, then build one that previews your latest issue, lets readers pick topics, and keeps the list yours.
fields.h1: Build a Newsletter Landing Page With a List You Own
fields.hero_description: Build a newsletter landing page that previews your latest issue and saves every subscriber to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Happens Between Signup and First Issue
fields.features_subheading: A newsletter landing page has one job: turning a visitor into a subscriber. These six parts handle the signup and what comes after it.
fields.feature_1:
Describe the newsletter, get the page

Describe who reads the newsletter, how often it goes out, and what to ask at signup. Emergent builds the page and the subscriber table, then changes any part when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
Every subscriber is a row you own

Each signup saves the email, the date, the form answers, and the link the reader came from. The rows sit in a database you own, and the list stays yours when you change email tools.
fields.feature_3:
New subscribers reach your email tool

Built apps connect to any tool with an API. Each new subscriber and their tags can sync to the platform you send issues from, and edits made there can sync back to your table.
fields.feature_4:
Questions that sort readers at signup

Ask for a role, a region, or the sections a reader wants, and each answer saves as a tag on the row. Stop at one or two questions and keep the email field as the main ask.
fields.feature_5:
Signups counted as they arrive

The dashboard behind the page shows signups live, split by source link and by confirmation status. Run a podcast mention against a social post for 2 weeks and keep the stronger one.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain now, your code later

Publish the page on your own domain; custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository for a developer to extend.

fields.tab_content_1:
Readers see this week's 3 headlines before signing up

Haulpoint Weekly goes out every Tuesday to freight brokers. Its landing page lists this week's 3 headlines above the form, then asks for an email and a role. Dorian Vesk signed up as a carrier, one of 38 signups this week.
fields.tab_content_2:
Of 4 sections, Sunniva Paskal reads the 2 she picked

Brinecove Table covers food in a coastal town across 4 sections: Openings, Markets, Recipes, and Events. Readers tick the ones they want when they sign up. Sunniva Paskal ticked Openings and Markets, and her row saved with those 2 tags, which sync to the email tool Brinecove sends from.
fields.tab_content_3:
7 of 54 signups still wait on the confirm link

Pellwick Studio sends one letter a month about its ceramics classes. Each signup saves as Pending, and the app sends a confirm link through the studio's email tool. A click turns the row to Confirmed. This month, 47 of 54 signups are confirmed and 7 are still pending.
fields.tab_content_4:
Velma Ambrose gets the guide after 3 confirmed referrals

Fernrow Notes is a weekly gardening newsletter. Its thank-you screen gives each new subscriber a personal referral link. Once 3 people a subscriber referred have confirmed, the seed-starting guide goes out through the email tool. Velma Ambrose reached 3 confirmed referrals, and the guide is in her inbox.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Newsletter Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow seven steps to create a newsletter landing page that shows readers what they get and saves every confirmed signup.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what one issue gives a reader
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Lead the headline with the result
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Show a real issue above the form
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask for the email plus one answer
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write one sentence on what a reader gets from each issue and how often it arrives, such as freight rate news every Tuesday. That sentence feeds the headline and the welcome email, and it stops the page from promising more than the issues deliver.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Say what the reader walks away with, not the format. "The freight rates that moved this week" says more than "Join our newsletter". Use the line under it for the schedule and the time an issue takes to read, such as a 4-minute read every Tuesday.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put the writing itself on the page, either the latest headlines or a short excerpt from last week's issue. Let a visitor judge the newsletter before you ask for an email, and link the archive for anyone who wants more than one sample.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Keep the form to the email field plus one question that changes what you send, like the reader's role. Leave the name field off unless your issues greet readers by name, and skip any question you will not use within a month.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell Emergent the newsletter's name, who it is for, the form questions, and what happens after a signup. Emergent turns that into the page, with a table for every subscriber behind it. Add a confirm step or rewrite the headline later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send a test signup through every path
fields.howto_step_6_des: Sign up with a test address for each role or section on the form, and once more without clicking the confirm link. Check that every row saves with the right tags, and that only the signups whose link was clicked turn Confirmed.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Connect your email tool and publish
fields.howto_step_7_des: Connect the tool you send issues from and check that a test subscriber arrives there with its tags. Then go live on your own domain (built into Emergent, uses credits) and put the link in your email signature and on every profile where you mention the newsletter.

faq_plan.q: What is a newsletter landing page?
faq_plan.a: A newsletter landing page is a standalone web page with one goal: getting a visitor to subscribe to a newsletter. It says what each issue covers and how often it arrives, then asks for an email address, with no menu or other offer competing for the click.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a newsletter landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the newsletter to Emergent's AI landing page builder: who it is for and what should happen after someone signs up. Emergent builds the page and a subscriber database you own, and you change any part by prompting again. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in newsletter landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: Look at what each page shows before the email field. The newsletter landing page examples worth copying put a sample of the writing on the page, such as recent headlines, and state the schedule in plain words. Then count the form fields and check whether a confirm step follows the signup, which a screenshot will not show you.

faq_plan.q: When does a newsletter landing page template help?
faq_plan.a: It helps when the layout is what slows you down. A newsletter landing page template fixes the look, but the tags and the sync to your email tool still have to be built. The form here is shorter than on a lead generation landing page, sometimes only the email. Emergent builds the page and its subscriber table from one prompt, with no template to adapt.

faq_plan.q: What should a subscribe landing page ask for besides an email?
faq_plan.a: One question at most, and only if the answer changes what you send. A role or a choice of sections works on a subscribe landing page, because each answer can decide which issues a reader gets. Ask nothing you will not use. The app Emergent builds keeps every answer with the email in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Is a landing page for newsletter signups better than a signup box on my homepage?
faq_plan.hint: What is an email newsletter landing page?
faq_plan.a: Use both. A dedicated landing page for newsletter signups gives you one link to share in a podcast or a guest post, and nothing on it competes with the subscribe button. The homepage box catches visitors who are already on your site. Track the two as separate sources to see which one brings in readers.

faq_plan.q: How long should a newsletter landing page be?
faq_plan.a: Short: one phone screen for the headline and the form, plus a sample of the writing. A squeeze page cuts everything except the headline and the form. For a newsletter, leave room near the form for a few recent headlines or an excerpt, since readers judge a newsletter by its writing.

faq_plan.q: How does a confirm link work on a newsletter landing page?
faq_plan.a: The new signup waits as pending while an email with a link goes out; the address counts as a subscriber only once its owner clicks it. That keeps mistyped and typed-in fake addresses from counting. Use it if you care more about who reads than about the raw count, and send one reminder before you drop an unconfirmed signup.

faq_plan.q: Should a newsletter landing page show the subscriber count?
faq_plan.a: Show it once the number helps, and leave it off until then. A count in the thousands tells a visitor that other people chose this newsletter; a count of 40 can say the opposite. An app built with Emergent can show the count live from the subscriber table, and the figure on the page stays current.

faq_plan.q: How do I track which links bring visitors to my newsletter landing page?
faq_plan.a: Add a source tag to every link you share, such as ?src=podcast, and save it with each signup. Compare confirmed signups by source after 2 weeks rather than raw clicks. The same tag works on a lead capture form elsewhere on your site, and every row in the table then carries where it came from.

plan.angle: The top 10 is example galleries (beehiiv, Inbox Collective, Sotion, Dribbble, Pinterest) and email platform feature pages (Mailchimp, CleverReach, MailPoet); they show the page but stop at the email field. This page shows four newsletter landing pages working after the signup: a weekly industry brief that previews its latest headlines and asks for a role, a local food newsletter where readers pick their sections, a studio's monthly letter that counts a reader only after the confirm link is clicked, and a gardening newsletter that sends a guide after 3 confirmed referrals. The FAQ answers what people building one ask about examples, templates, what to ask on the form, confirmation, length, headlines and tracking. Squeeze pages, lead generation pages and lead capture forms are siblings and stay out of the headings.
